utterances.text: And have you -- and has -- seen any particular problems that Jokic may be referring to at this time in the evening? Any idea what he is talking about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time on the 14th, you have a situation where they are still just finishing up, they're actually still executing prisoners at the Orahovac killing fields. They haven't quite started at Petkovci yet. They're still prisoners up to other locations. But, in context, you have the military column which has now broken through the first line of defence on the late evening of the 13th and is pushing actually relatively close to Orahovac and further on. So it's a mixed conversation where Jokic is trying to deal with issues and explain problems with the prisoners and, at the same time, they have a worse -- worsening military situation with respect to actual combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Was there any indication in the public testimony of Dragan Obrenovic in the Blagojevic case that Jokic informed him of any problems with the prisoners at some point? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a lot of years, sir. I don't think I recall anymore. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a while since I've read that testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's go to the next document, 65 ter 2996A. A one-line intercept that you've -- believed talked about many times over the years. We're now on the 15th of -- of July, according to this intercept. And it says: "Colonel Beara was looking for General Zivanovic, but he was not there. He said he was to call him at extension 139." What's -- what's going on here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a summary of a conversation where Colonel Beara is calling from a location looking for General Zivanovic, not reaching him immediately, and leaving a message that Zivanovic was to call him or could reach him - him being Colonel Beara - at extension 139.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall what extension 139 is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Extension 139 is the phone line for the phone in Drago Nikolic's office in the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 2996A shall be assigned Exhibit P2541. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just skip over the next one. It's another version of that. So let's go to 65 ter 2997B.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is, again, 15 July 1995, at 0954 hours, just two minutes after that last little one-line synopsis, and the participants are General Zivanovic and Colonel Ljubo Beara, according to the intercept operators. I won't read all of it. We see that there are some initial hellos and some comments. And then Beara noted as B says: "Okay then. Listen Bro." Zivanovic says: "Yes?" B says: "You know that day? I informed the commander about it. Furtula didn't send Lukic's intervention platoon." And Lukic is waiting at Blagojevic. Sorry, Zivanovic says: "And Lukic is waiting at Blagojevic." And then Beara says: "Lukic is here with me and his driver and we urged them on that." Can you tell us, based on your review of this entire intercept and the other information, what do you believe he is talking about and who are these people, the commander, for one; Furtula, for the other; Lukic and his intervention platoon, another? Who are these guys? What's he talking about in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Furtula is Major Radomir Furtula is the commander of the Visegrad Light Infantry Brigade. In this context Lukic has been identified by the investigation as Milan Lukic, and they're talking about instructions that his particular platoon was supposed to be sent up on the commander's orders. Again, in this context, I take the commander to be General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we haven't heard much about the Visegrad Brigade. What corps do they belong to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Visegrad Brigade is also part of the Drina Corps Command. Or part of the Drina Corps, more accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you remember its formalised name?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It should be the 5th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And Zivanovic says: "And Lukic is waiting at Blagojevic." What Blagojevic do you think he would mean in this context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagojevic being the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. He is trying to say that Lukic is supposedly waiting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters or somewhere in Bratunac where he can be reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Beara says: "Lukic is here with me and his driver and we urged them on that." And where do you think based on the context of these intercepts Beara is at this point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going back to the previous intercept, if he's asked for General Zivanovic to call him at 139, and General Zivanovic has called him there, then, at the time of this intercept, Colonel Beara is sitting in Drago Nikolic's office at the Zvornik Brigade headquarters. It's the Standard facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then Beara continues: "And yesterday Furtula sent one soldier without an arm and another one that Lukic knows as a drunkard." And then he says: "Fuck him." Zivanovic says: "Yes." Beara says: "Instead of a platoon." Zivanovic says: "Oh dear." Beara says: "Simply, he doesn't give a damn about the commander's orders [sic]. Well, now that platoon has 60 men." Who do you think Beara is referring to when he says "commanders" here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe, again in this context, the commander he is referring to is General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Then Zivanovic says something we can't hear. Beara says: "Have him send at least half." Zivanovic says: "Yes, yes." Beara says: "Say again?" Zivanovic: "To send them immediately. "Yes." And then Zivanovic says: "I can't order that anymore." What do you take Zivanovic's comment about "I can't order that anymore" to refer to; and do you have an opinion on why he is saying that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. What Zivanovic is doing is, in this case, informing or reminding Colonel Beara that since he is no longer the commander of the Drina Corps, he has no authority or right to issue commands to subordinate brigade commanders, or -- because they're not his subordinates anymore, in that nature. So he's just saying I'm no longer empowered to make orders like that, and when you look at the next line he is basically giving Beara a phone extension to call.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who do you believe that phone extension is? We see 385.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 385 is the phone extension associated with the Drina Corps commander. Not only in Vlasenica, but when the Drina Corps commander is in a different location, for example, at a forward command post, if they're going to be there for a few days, they will actually trunk -- electronically trunk that line so it rings out wherever the corps commander is located. You call 385, you're going to get whomever the corps commander is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we'll get to this in a minute, but is there another intercept right after this between Beara and Krstic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Explain, if you will, how it is a colonel like Beara, who you say the evidence indicates is at the Zvornik Brigade, how is it that he is calling up and asking General Zivanovic for troops? He is a colonel, he is from the Main Staff, he is the chief of security. Can you explain how, in your view, this works in the military, the appropriate military context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As I've frequently noted, officers performing their duties are going to give the orders that they're lawfully entitled to give. In many cases, they will be supplemental orders to a broader order that they have received. In this manner, you have Colonel Beara having a discussion with General Zivanovic. From this particular intercept, it's clear that both of them understand what the commander's orders were and that various units of the Drina Corps were supposed to send, in this case, at least one intervention unit, in furtherance of the commander's orders. And, in this case, the commander being General Mladic. So it's not improper for Colonel Beara to call General Zivanovic, particularly since, in this conversation, Colonel Beara is -- is unaware that General Zivanovic, for whatever -- you know, at this point can't give orders like that anymore. It's -- it's not improper for Colonel Beara to call General Zivanovic to remind him of what General Mladic's orders were in this issue and to ask General Zivanovic to give the necessary orders to his brigade commander to ensure that General Mladic's orders are carried out as he gave them. That is an appropriate role for what a staff officer would do in furtherance of ensuring his commander's orders are fully carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why couldn't, under these rules, Beara, as a colonel, just order the troops from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because General -- or because Colonel Beara does not have the right to command those soldiers from the Zvornik Brigade. That right is vested solely in the brigade commander. Or, at this point in time, the brigade deputy commander. The fact that Colonel Beara is following the boss's orders does not give him unlimited authority to command soldiers from other units. He has to exercise proper command and staff channels and relationships. Colonel Beara is within his rights to relay to Colonel Zivanovic that General Mladic's orders are not being followed and that General Zivanovic should give the orders necessary to ensure that General Mladic's orders are complied with. But Colonel Beara does not, in and of himself, possess the authority to bypass General Zivanovic or, as you'll see in the next intercept, General Krstic, and directly contact or phone down to the 5th Podrinje Unit and order Major Furtula to send that platoon immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd offer this intercept into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 2997B shall be assigned Exhibit P2542. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So now if we could go to P506B. It's the same date, 15 July. The time is now 10.00, about five or six minutes after the last one. Bless you. The participants are noted. Colonel Ljubo Beara and -- bless you. Colonel Ljubo Beara and General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see Beara saying: "General, Furtula didn't carry out the boss's order." Who do you think the boss is in this context?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we're talking about the exact same context of the last intercept, the boss is General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Krstic says: "Listen, he ordered him to lead out a tank, not a train." Beara says: "But I need 30 men, just like it was ordered." Then Krstic says: "Take from Nastic or Blagojevic." Who do you believe Krstic is referring to when he says Nastic or Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagojevic is the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Nastic is the commander of the Milici Light Infantry Brigade. So what he is telling Beara to do is he is authorising Beara to contact those two units and have them pull -- have them send the people as requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Krstic doesn't suggest Pandurevic or Obrenovic. Any reason why he wouldn't have in that situation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By this time, 1000 hours on 15 July, General Krstic is now well aware of the dire military situation in the Zvornik municipality, and, in fact, has already sent back Colonel Pandurevic and the two battalions worth of soldiers -- or the two tactical groups worth of soldiers from Zepa to return back to Zvornik so they can militarily deal with the column. So clearly, knowing that -- General Krstic is not -- knowing what's happening in Zvornik, he is not going to suggest that troops be taken from the combat line in Zvornik. He is basically saying take them from units that are less militarily involved right now and, you know, basically identifying the Bratunac Brigade or the Milici Brigade as possible sources of those troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: After suggesting Nastic and Blagojevic, Krstic goes on so say: "I can't pull anything out of here for you." Where is Krstic at the time; and what is he doing?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of this intercept, General Krstic is at the IKM, I believe, it's pronounced Krivace, and is engaged in the military operations related to Zepa. So, again this is an example of what I mean, how they've run extension 385 out to the forward command post so it can reach General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Would that IKM be Krivace?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's a more accurate pronunciation of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And then Beara says: "But I don't have any here. I need them today and I'll give them back tonight. Krle, you have to understand, I can't explain it to you, like this." What's this term, "Krle"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krle was a nickname that various senior officers had for General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when he says "I can't explain it to you like this," what's your view of what that mean, if anything?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, he's -- as the chief of Main Staff, the security administration, he probably knows better than anyone else the vulnerabilities of the telephone system to potential compromise and is making it clear, I can't really go into the details of the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Krstic says: "I'll disturb everything on his axis if I pull them out, and a lot depends on him." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Visegrad Brigade was involved in the Zepa operation, coming in from a separate angle from the main attack. Part of the military operation for these units was to draw forces away or keep forces pinned down so the main forces attacking from the north would find less resistance in this context, basically what General Krstic is telling Beara is that, I can't weaken that particular axis of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then Beara says: "I can't resolve anything without ..." and that should read 15 to 30 men. That's a misprint in the English translation. And Boban Indjic is how it is spelled in the B/C/S, not Djindjic. Do you know who this Boban Indjic was at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. He's a member of the Visegrad Brigade. And actually at this time he is a subordinate to Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall an intercept on the 13th that had something to do with a unit with -- from Visegrad coming up to the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do. If I recall correctly, the intercept notes that they were on their way but due to a mechanical problem the bus carrying them broke down, so they could not complete the journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I believe that's in evidence, but I will check on that intercept. All right. So Beara says: "I can't resolve anything without 15, 30 men, and Boban Indjic." Krstic says: "Ljubo, this is not protected." Beara says: "I know, I know." What's going on here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, now General Krstic is reminding Beara that this particular line is liable to intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then Krstic says: "I will see what I can do but it will disturb a lot. Have a look down there at Nastic and Blagojevic's." I think that's self-explanatory. Beara says: "But I don't have any. If I did, I wouldn't still be asking for the third day." Krstic says: "Again, check with Blagojevic. Take his Red Berets." What are the Red Berets, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Red Berets unit was an intervention platoon, part of the Bratunac Brigade. Normally it was assigned to the 3rd Infantry Battalion but because most of the particular individuals to that unit were younger and fitter soldiers, they were often used in a number of other places during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, we see what Beara says about that, "they're not there. They took off." I won't repeat it all. Krstic again says: "I will see what I can do." Beara says: "Check it out and have them go to Drago's." In this context, who is Drago and where is Drago's, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago is Drago Nikolic, the chief of security for the Zvornik Brigade. If Beara is telling them to go to Drago's, they're -- what he is basically saying is, Send them to the headquarters of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, have them report to Drago Nikolic where I happen to be sitting at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Krstic says: "I can't guarantee anything." Beara responds: "Krle, I don't know what to do anymore." Krstic says: "Ljubo, then take those MUP men from up there." What's that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we've discussed over the last couple of days, there were a number of MUP units who were under military command related to this operation and in this context, General Krstic is throwing out the idea of potentially MUP or police officers being used by Beara for his task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Beara responds: "No, they won't do anything. I talked ..." That's fairly self-explanatory. And then he says there is no other solution but for the 15 to 30 men with Indjic. The thing that was supposed to arrive on the 13th but didn't. Krstic says: "Ljubo, have you to understand me too...," then "you've done fucking all sorts to me. Then Beara says: "I understand, but have you to understand me too, and had ... these men [sic] been done then, we wouldn't be arguing over it now." What do these exchanges mean to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic is obviously not happy about having to figure out where he's going to find additional people for the task that Beara is undertaking, and Beara is reminding him that, had the people showed up like they were supposed to, we wouldn't be having this conversation today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So now Krstic says: "Fuck it. Now I'll be the one to blame." Blamed for what, in your view? What is Krstic being worried about being blamed for?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that given what Colonel Beara is involved in, General Krstic is worried about the fact that he will get blamed because the executions that are supposed to be occurring are taking longer than they're suppose to because individuals who were supposed to be sent haven't been send. Now he is the corps commander. The fact that they weren't sent from the Visegrad Brigade ultimately is his responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Beara responds: "I don't know what to do. I mean it, Krle. There are still 3500 parcels that I have to distribute and I have no solution." What do you take it -- this term "3500 parcels to distribute" means? What are the parcels?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The parcels in this particular context is the euphemism that they were using for prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see this intercept is at 10.00 a.m. on the 15th. Do you remember what prisoners are still alive in the Zvornik Brigade area of responsibility at 10.00 a.m. on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, by this time, the prisoners from the Orahovac school and the Petkovci school have already been killed, but there are still prisoners alive in Rocevic and Pilica, as well as the overflow prisoners that are going into the Dom of Kulture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so in that context, when Beara says this, and this it's this -- "that I have to distribute and I have no solution." What does he mean by, "that I have to distribute and I have no solution"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's, in my opinion, a clear reference to the fact that these prisoners have to die and at the moment he doesn't have the means to undertake executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. The other version of that intercept which is already in evidence so I won't go there. Let's go to 65 ter 114. We're still in our chronology. And what we have here is a document from a person named Colonel Ignjat Milanovic. I'll remind the Trial Chamber, you have heard General Keserovic talk about this document a bit, but it was a while back. And this is 15 July. It is entitled: "Engagement of Forces in Searching the Terrain in the Direction of Zepa and the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade." Thank you for getting that handwritten version up for us. I think that they should be in the binder. It's entitled: "Proposal." And the proposal is to authorise and appoint the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade to command all the forces searching the terrain. Can you just give us a synopsis briefly of what's going on here and who this Ignjat Milanovic is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Ignjat Milanovic is an officer on the Drina Corps Command. His normal role is that he is the chief of the air and air defence forces for the corps. What this particular document is, is a reflection of a normal and often-exercised practice of the VRS of sending various staff officers to locations in order to gain a clear picture of what's going on and to ensure various orders are being forwarded -- sorry, followed and were necessary to make proposals for changes in orders if the circumstances change. In this context, he is replying that, based on the order of the Drina Corps commander, I went to these various locations and acquainted myself with the situation. He is now reporting back to the Drina Corps commander and saying, Here are the things that I of my own authorities have ordered based on what he believes he is authorised to give orders against. And then he makes an additional proposal related to some various command resubordinations, which clearly he doesn't believe he is authorised to undertake, and needs the approval of the Drina Corps Command. So this is a relatively typical role that a staff officer would play in the context of a military operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And does - one last question - this proposal have anything to do with the column and the Muslims from Srebrenica that you had been talking about, that moved through the area earlier?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, in the sense that these are the remnants, the back end of the column that had been cut off by the 13th of July and in subsequent days, the 14th and 15th, they're still engaged in operations against them. And what is apparent to Colonel Milanovic under the circumstances is that they're having problems with successfully dealing with the battle because the various military forces that are engaged in it are under independent commands and that he believes that because there's not one overall commander, co-ordinating this situation and directing the activities of the units, that they're not being as successful as they should be in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does that include MUP units?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There, at this point in time, there were still two companies of the Jahorina MUP on the road between Sandici and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And do you recall their -- their immediate commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their immediate commander was Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And his subordinate commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this case, it would be Mendelav Djuric and Nedjo Ikonic -- I'm sorry, Dusko Jevic. And then below him would be Mendelav Djuric and Nedjo Ikonic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what officer was Milanovic proposing take over command of all these units?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: His proposal was that it was the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who was?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I would offer that -- that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received. But I would like to ask you to repeat one answer. Page 62, lines -- line 16. You have mentioned several names which are not recorded. Could you please repeat them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The question was related to the subordinate commanders of Ljubisa Borovcanin, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next subordinate commander would be Dusko Jevic, and then subordinate to Dusko Jevic were the two actual company commanders, Mendelav Djuric and Nedjo Ikonic. That's I-k-o-n-i-c, N-e-d-j-o.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I guess we have gone past the break five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have it on the screen. Thank you. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 114 shall be assigned exhibit number P2543.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We must have our next break now, and we will resume 20 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the outset of today's hearing, you, Mr. McCloskey, indicated a change of status of three documents. The Chamber checked these indications, looked into the details, and I can confirm that P2304 should now be public. Instead of that, P2337 and P2298 should be under seal. Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Butler, let's now go to P2218. We left off with the last document, the proposal by Colonel Milanovic for Colonel Blagojevic to take over command of these units searching this terrain coming out of the enclave area. Now we can see we actually have a document. It's a daily combat report in the name of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Blagojevic. From his command to the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Blagojevic, from his command to the command of the Drina Corps. And while it doesn't say anything specific on that point, we do see in the middle of paragraph 2, we've got the handwritten version, there's also a typed version in the B/C/S, but we see in the middle of paragraph 2 it says: "During the day the brigade commander visited all units which are blocking the enemy retreat." And it lists all these different units, brigades, the 65th Protection Regiment; the Milici Brigade, the 65th Protection Regiment, parts of the MUP, and the 5th Engineering Battalion. And it says he defined their tasks and organised their joint action and communications. What do you make of that, that the brigade commander did this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to slow down again. Because some parts of your reading into the record is missing. Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In this particular document, it reflects that the proposal made by Colonel Milanovic the day prior has been, to a large degree, accepted by the Drina Corps commander, General Krstic, and subsequently he'd ordered Colonel Blagojevic, the Bratunac Brigade commander, to implement these as far as at least visiting all of the units, defining their tasks, and organising their joint actions and communications. Does not specifically say take command, but clearly Colonel Blagojevic has been given an order to all to synchronise all of the operations of these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, if the next day, the 17th, Colonel Blagojevic was sent off to Zepa at some point, what situation would that create, if these units were -- were still searching the area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would, in effect, be the same situation that was in existence on the 15th, and there would be a requirement for somebody else to take control of synchronising all of these units and integrating their operations against the remnants of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go now to P -- it's 126. This is a document we spent some time with, with another witness, but let me ask you a bit about it, Mr. Butler. We see that it's from the Main Staff. 17 July. And we see that it's in the name of Ratko Mladic. And the entitled: "Integrating of Operations to Crush Lagging Muslim Forces." And it's to the Drina Corps command for information and to the Zvornik Brigade, the Bratunac Brigade, the Milici Brigade, and the 67th Communications Regiment. And the first paragraph talks about sending three officers, and it names them, from the Main Staff to assist -- to the Zvornik Brigade, and I'll read it slowly: "To assist in the joining of the VRS and MUP forces, the planning and co-ordination of combat operations to block, crush, and destroy lagging Muslim forces in the wider area of Kamenica and Cerska." Can you tell us, if you recall, who these people were, Colonels Nedjo Trkulja?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of armoured forces for the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Milovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was another intelligence officer with the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Under who?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that context, he would be under General Tolimir. Although, more accurately, under Colonel Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Bogdan Sladojevic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an officer who had just been reassigned from the federal army, the VJ, to the VRS, and he was on temporary duty at the Main Staff before assuming his job as the chief of operations for the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. He just happened to be there at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please, Mr. President, could you instruct Mr. McCloskey to give us the reference where it shows that that officer was subordinated to me. If they were deployed pursuant to an order issued by somebody else, where does it say that he was subordinated to Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, that was the answer of the witness and not any suggestion of Mr. McCloskey to the witness. Mr. McCloskey just asked who was that person. Please carry on Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the context was this: Who would that person have been subordinated to? That's what Mr. McCloskey asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to you, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you may deal with that during your cross-examination. It is absolutely correct and there's no criticism if Mr. McCloskey asks who a certain person is subordinated to. That's all. And that is an absolutely correct question. Please carry on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, do you recall upon which document or authority or -- you base your opinion regarding the placement of Milovan Stankovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a while. I'd have to research that myself. But to be clear, I'm not implying that in this order that Milovan Stankovic was sent to the Zvornik Brigade on the order of General Tolimir. I'm just noting that Milovan Stankovic is an intelligence officer with the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And this says, number 2: "The team from the VRS ... shall assess the situation on the brigade's front line and in the rear, the available forces, and hear out the proposal and opinion of the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. On this basis, they are to draw up a plan together with the brigade commander to comb the terrain, block, crush, and destroy the straggling parts of the [sic] armed Muslim groups in the wider areas of Kamenica, Cerska, and Udrc." Now, we have jumped a little bit ahead of our chronology because of the second part of this document and the previous documents we've been related to. But can you put these two paragraphs into context? What -- what had gone on in the Zvornik Brigade area, in terms of the military situation, and what, in your view, based on your review of the materials, do 1 and 2 have to do with?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I previously discussed, the military situation in the Zvornik Brigade, on 16 July 1995, and the combat that was occurring with the column, Colonel Pandurevic made an agreement with the commander of the 28th Infantry -- or not the commander, I'm sorry, with Semso Muminovic to allow the column to pass through the lines and into Bosnian Muslim-held territory. As noted, that was not an act that was authorised by either the Drina Corps Command or the Main Staff, and as word spread that Colonel Pandurevic had made this agreement, there are various documents, intercepts, which reflect that a lot of people were very disturbed by hearing this. The following day, this -- these two paragraphs reflect General Mladic wanting to send and, in fact, he did send these three officers to talk to Pandurevic, and they also spoke to Obrenovic, in order to make an independent evaluation of the situation and later potentially make a recommendation back to General Mladic what, if any, actions might be taken against Colonel Pandurevic for his decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you aware of any negative recommendation or action that was taken against Pandurevic for his decision to open up the corridor?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. And, in fact, when I discussed earlier the 18 July interim combat report, I had noted that there was a bit of a back story to why Colonel Pandurevic felt a need to lay out a detailed accounting of not only his actions with respect to the most recent combat but the previous burdens that the Zvornik Brigade had been asked to shoulder. That interim report to General Krstic was motivated, to a large degree, by the visits of these three officers, and Colonel Pandurevic's feeling that he needed to really lay out his case and wanted to make it directly to General Krstic. In any event, for whatever reason, General Mladic did not sanction or relieve Colonel Pandurevic for his decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now let's take a look at paragraph 3 that speaks: "As of 17 July," and then it lists these forces, the Bratunac Brigade, and I won't list all of them. But are those the same forces that were spoken about by Ignjat Milanovic and in Blagojevic's daily combat report that we've just seen on this same topic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And it talks about discovering and destroying the lagging Muslim groups in this area. And it says: "I hereby appoint Lieutenant-Colonel Keserovic, the officer of the military police of the [sic] Main Staff security administration, as the commander of all the aforementioned forces." And then it gives it various other tasks related to that. And if, in fact, Colonel Blagojevic left the area on the 17th of July, would this order fill in that gap that you spoke of previously?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now let's go to 65 ter 249. This is a document from the command of the Bratunac Brigade on 17 July to the Drina Corps Command. It is in the name of Colonel Blagojevic, and it says: "Among the Muslim prisoners, there are four underage children (aged between 8 and 14) who are being held in a military custody in Bratunac. One of them told the commander of the unit that was searching the area about a large number of Muslim troops committing suicide or killing each other. We propose that this testimony be recorded by cameras of your press centre." Now, this reference to "units searching the area," do you connect this "units searching the area" reference with any -- any of the information set out in the previous document where Keserovic is put in command of the forces regarding the lagging Muslims from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The Bratunac Brigade forces, who were engaged in these activities, would have been under his direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you describe what you recall, if anything, about what -- what the forces did that day, on the 17th, that resulted in these prisoners? Just roughly. If you recall.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand from the investigation that a composite unit of the Bratunac Infantry Brigade and the MUP forces of the Jahorina MUP companies, on the 16th and 17th, were conducting sweep operations. And I believe that individuals who participated in this talk about, somewhere, of approximately 180 Bosnian Muslim men from that particular sweep operation being captured. Among them were these four underage, or four children.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I would offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter document 249 shall be assigned Exhibit P2544. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Getting back to our chronology, which is really on the 15th of July. We could go to P13, if we could. And this is the interim combat report from Vinko Pandurevic from the Zvornik Brigade to the Drina Corps Command. It's got a sent/received stamp of 1925 hours. Can you -- before we get into this document, can you set the scene for us? The early evening hours of 15 July. Where was Pandurevic that day, and what is he doing, as far as you know, from the investigation in this early -- at this time that this document was drafted and sent to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. As I've testified earlier, during the early morning hours of the 15th of July, Colonel Pandurevic and the two tactical groups that made up the formations of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade were directed to go from the Zepa battle-front and return to Zvornik, in order to deal with the unfolding military issue they were having. He arrived approximately 11.30, and by 12.00 was meeting with individuals at the Zvornik Brigade and other units that were involved - Major Obrenovic, Mr. Borovcanin, Dragomir Vasic - and discussed how they came together, and that Colonel Pandurevic had laid out a plan by which he wanted to block the column. This document is his interim combat report reflecting, in part, what the situation was in the Zvornik Brigade, what orders he had given, and at the time that he's drafting this, he is at his forward command post where he is co-ordinating the larger defence operations against the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And these first three paragraphs that describe the situation, did you find them to be roughly accurate when comparing various other reports and information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe this is a -- an accurate recounting of the information that everyone was aware of at the time on 15 July with respect to the battle-field situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So he -- in that third paragraph, talks about the attack on Memici is still in progress, that all targets deep inside the territory and the suburbs and town of Zvornik have been under artillery fire. Who can hit them with artillery fire at that point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be artillery fired from the positions of the ABiH 2 Corps on the other side of the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "All attacks have been repulsed successfully so far. So far, according to information received we have four dead and a dozen or so wounded. "With all available forces, we have sealed off the wider area of Crni Vrh and Planinci, and partially the area of Kamenica. "All brigade forces are fully engaged and we have no reserves." Now this next small paragraph I want to ask you about. It says: "An additional burden for us is the large number of prisoners distributed throughout schools in the brigade area, as well as obligations of security and restoration of terrain."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, it says: "... as well as obligations of security and 'asanacija terena,'" which is a term you've heard before which got translated as "restoration of the terrain." Now, this large number of prisoners distributed throughout the schools in the brigade area, by 7.00 p.m., the evening of 15 July, are there any prisoners alive at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Save the four survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, they are all dead except for the survivors there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were being killed during the day on the 15th. I don't know that we have any survivor accounts which reflect how late that was going on, but by 7.00 p.m. most of them should have been dead already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the Kula school in Pilica and the cultural centre in Pilica on the evening of 15 July, can you remind us what their status was based on the investigation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The group -- the groups at Pilica and at the Dom of culture were still alive and being detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what do you believe that Pandurevic is referring to when he says: "An additional burden for us is a large number of prisoners distributed throughout the schools in the brigade area, as well as obligations of security and 'asanacija terena'"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that Colonel Pandurevic understood within the context of what was happening that the requirements to, first, guard the prisoners, deal with their executions, and then to burry the bodies, as well as continuing to guard the prisoners at Pilica and the Dom of culture was having an adverse impact on his ability to deal with the combat situation which was occurring at the same time. The key phrase is that all brigade forces are fully engaged and we have -- he has no reserves. These forces that could have been available had they not been involved in these activity would have potentially given Colonel Pandurevic at least a minimal reserve force, but it was otherwise engaged on what were, you know, the tasks relating to prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you say "obligations of security," how is it that you say that this is guarding the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, the actual identities of who was responsible for the executions is still a little unclear. I am aware that members of the 4th Infantry Battalion in Orahovac were involved in the executions at that site. I do not know whether or not 6th Battalion members were involved in the executions at Petkovci; although, they were clearly involved in guarding the prisoners at the school. Most of the investigative work related to Rocevic occurred after departed from the ICTY and the Office of the Prosecutor, so I don't know that I'm fully clear on all of the elements that were involved in the executions at Rocevic, although I am aware that some members of potentially the 5th or 2nd Battalion were involved. And while the killings that were done at Branjevo were done by a combination of the 10th Sabotage Detachment and later on a group of men who had come up from Bratunac. And then later the final killings at the Dom of cultural which I'm not sure at this date who ultimately was responsible for executing those. But again, with respect to the 1st Battalion, they were engaged in the process of guarding them as well as the process of having to remove the bodies, particularly from the Dom of culture since it was in the middle of the town at Pilica, and bring them to where they would be buried at Branjevo. So again in that particular context it's all a reflection of the numbers of soldiers and units that had some involvement in the whole wider aspect of the crime or multiple crimes in this case. At the same time, there's also a pitched battle going on in other locations of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, it's -- there's a translation issue here. And it's the position of the Prosecution that the term "obligations of security" has to do with securing or guarding the prisoners, that the term related to security branch is a different term, and so it would not be appropriate to view this as obligations of the security branch. I believe Mr. Gajic and General Tolimir will agree with us on that. It's been the subject of agreement for many years. But, of course, I'll wait to hear from them on that. There's a bit more time to discuss this document, Mr. President. We can talk about it tomorrow or finish it tonight, whatever is -- you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we have to adjourn for today. You may continue tomorrow. We are sitting in the afternoon. Therefore, we resume at 2.15 in the afternoon in this courtroom, number III. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of July, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.
